sources.title: Deploy a hosted agent: handler, platform identity and injected variables
sources.note: Documents ResponsesAgentServerHost, the three-argument async response handler, dedicated agent identity and platform-injected Foundry variables. The desktop deployment identity is not the runtime agent identity.

sources.title: Deploy a hosted agent from source code
sources.note: Documents python_3_13, main.py, requirements.txt, remote_build, existing project ID and code-deployment init flags. Use the sample's Responses 2.0.0 protocol, not the older 1.0.0 value in some REST examples.

sources.title: Official Foundry Agent Framework sample at a fixed commit
sources.note: Verified main.py, requirements.txt and azure.yaml. This sample has no pyproject.toml. It uses Agent, FoundryChatClient, DefaultAzureCredential and store=False. Our original handler and explicit telemetry wiring are not a copy of the sample.

sources.title: Official Responses pyproject sample at the same commit
sources.note: Verified Python >=3.13, azure-ai-agentserver-responses==2.1.0 and azure-identity==1.25.3. Its older azure-ai-projects==2.0.1 is not used: the current FoundryChatClient requires >=2.2.0 and <2.7.0.

sources.title: Agent 365 data-collection scope for hosted agents
sources.note: Hosted agents must package and configure the SDK. Explicit hosted SDK configuration overrides Foundry resource-level disablement. a365LoggingEnabled is not this sample's export kill switch.

sources.title: Grant Agent 365 observability permissions
sources.note: The deployed agentIdentityId is the principal object ID. Fixed appRoleId: 8f71190c-00c8-461d-a63b-f74abde9ba52. Our script strengthens the example by resolving the resource service principal by application ID and checking the role value, type and enabled state.

sources.title: Microsoft OpenTelemetry Python 1.3.9 source
sources.note: Verified InvokeAgentScope, ExecuteToolScope, Request, AgentDetails, explicit scope error capture, SDKStats switches and direct _Agent365Exporter constructor. The direct exporter is internal and is deliberately pinned; inspect it before upgrades. No legacy standalone observability package is used.

sources.title: Published Microsoft OpenTelemetry package metadata
sources.note: Published version and dependency metadata checked. Requires OpenTelemetry SDK/API ~=1.44.0. No dependency installation or telemetry export was performed for this hosted sample.

sources.title: Published Foundry Agent Framework package metadata
sources.note: Requires agent-framework-core >=1.17.0,<2, agent-framework-openai >=1.14.2,<2 and azure-ai-projects >=2.2.0,<2.7.0. The selected direct pins satisfy these ranges.

sources.title: Published Responses protocol package metadata
sources.note: Requires azure-ai-agentserver-core >=2.1.0,<2.2.0. Source inspected at azure-ai-agentserver-responses_2.1.0.

sources.title: Pinned Responses context API
sources.note: Verified conversation_chain_id, platform_context.call_id, get_input_text and shutdown. The opaque call ID is forwarded to the model and is not parsed or exported as caller identity.

sources.title: Pinned AgentServer host telemetry configuration
sources.note: configure_observability=None disables SDK-managed observability setup. Default behavior otherwise uses the injected Application Insights connection string. The accompanying _tracing.py documents api://9b975845-388f-4429-889e-eab1ef63949c/.default for hosted A365.

sources.title: Agent Framework Python 1.18.0 source
sources.note: Verified sticky disable_instrumentation, Agent async context lifecycle, agent.run client_kwargs, FoundryChatClient and OpenAI extra_headers/max_tokens mapping. The code awaits actual model execution; mocked tests do not prove model access.

sources.title: Azure Identity DefaultAzureCredential
sources.note: Credential exclusion flags prevent developer and environment-secret fallback. The hosted sample leaves only workload and managed identity paths. A hosted platform token must still pass explicit tenant, audience and appID consistency checks.

sources.title: Pinned azd agent init help
sources.note: Verified --manifest, --project-id, --model-deployment, --agent-name, --deploy-mode, --runtime and --entry-point. The same snapshot distinguishes an existing deployment from --model, which can create a new model. azd is not installed locally; this is upstream help-source verification, not an executed CLI validation.

sources.title: Pinned azd provision and deploy help
sources.note: Verified TestUsage-azd-provision.snap (--preview) and TestUsage-azd-deploy.snap (positional service name). Agent show help at the same commit supports a service name and --output json.

sources.title: Pinned Foundry manifest schema implementation and substitution
sources.note: An azure.ai.project endpoint selects an existing project. No deployments block is included. cli/azd/pkg/foundry/templating.go at the same commit verifies ${VAR:-default} syntax. Manifest shape was source-checked; no Azure service-side schema validation was performed.
